bu-summer-challenge-2027.about:
Summer Challenge is Boston University's two-week, non-credit pre-college programme for students entering their sophomore, junior or senior year. Each student takes one small, discussion-based seminar (past topics have included creative writing, engineering, entrepreneurship, psychology, public health and international relations), then joins daily activities, workshops and trips around Boston.

2027 residential sessions are 20 June–2 July, 11–23 July and 25 July–6 August (commuter sessions start the next day). It is a low-pressure way for younger students to try US campus life before committing to longer programmes such as BU's three-week Academic Immersion or six-week RISE.

In 2026 the total charge was US$5,245 residential (tuition, housing, meals and activities) or US$3,989 commuter, plus a US$75 application fee. BU states that no financial aid is available for Summer Challenge. International students can apply; BU publishes separate guidance for them.
highlights: Short, two-week introduction to US college life
Small seminars in a subject of your choice
Three 2027 session dates to fit school calendars
bu-summer-challenge-2027.eligibility: Students entering their sophomore, junior or senior year of high school in autumn 2027, from any country. Admission is based on grades, courses and a personal statement; international applicants may need to show English proficiency.
how_to_apply: Choose a seminar and session when the 2027 list is published
Open the application from 17 December 2026 (the student must submit it personally)
Upload your full transcript including fall 2026 grades and write the personal statement
Pay the US$75 application fee; after admission, pay the deposit to confirm
bu-summer-challenge-2027.costs: 2026 guide (2027 prices due 17 Dec 2026): residential US$5,245, commuter US$3,989 (tuition, materials and activities; residential includes housing and meals). Application fee US$75. No financial aid for Summer Challenge.

uwc-maastricht.about:
UWC Maastricht is a public, Dutch-government-subsidised UWC school in Maastricht, the Netherlands, close to the German and Belgian borders. It teaches pupils aged 4 to 19, but about 200 residential students aged 16 to 19 live on campus and follow either the IB Diploma Programme (IBDP) or the IB Career-related Programme (IBCP), one of only two UWCs that offer the IBCP. Students come from more than 100 nationalities.

The school runs a social-impact programme of action-oriented courses, social entrepreneurship, student-led conferences and community service, alongside the academic IB core (Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and CAS). The leafy campus is close to the city centre of one of the Netherlands' most visited cities.

For 2027 entry (studies start August 2027), most students are chosen by their UWC national committee, which also decides scholarships. Full fee-payers can apply via the Global Selection Programme, where UWC Maastricht sits in the USD 91,000 to 110,000 two-year fee band. It is a strong choice if you want a large, very international school in the heart of Europe with a career-related IB option.
highlights: One of only two UWCs offering the IB Career-related Programme as well as the IB Diploma
About 200 boarders from 100+ nationalities in a public Dutch school
Social-impact programme with social entrepreneurship and student-led conferences
uwc-maastricht.eligibility: Students aged about 16 to 19 at enrolment in August 2027 (exact birth-date window set by each national committee), usually in the last two years of secondary school. Open to every nationality: you apply through the UWC national committee of your citizenship or residence (more than 150 committees, e.g. Georgia, Jordan, Egypt, India), through the Global Selection Programme if you can pay full fees, or through the International Application Pathway if your country has no committee and you need financial aid (relevant for many Gulf nationals, e.g. Qatar, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman, which have no UWC committee). You may submit only one UWC application per entry year. Good working English is needed; fluency is not required at application.

uwc-robert-bosch-college.about:
UWC Robert Bosch College (UWC RBC) in Freiburg, Germany, is a joint project of the Deutsche Stiftung UWC and the Robert Bosch Stiftung. About 200 students aged 16 to 19 from more than 90 countries, speaking over 60 languages, live together and follow the two-year IB Diploma Programme with average class sizes of 12.

Deliberate diversity is the college's main goal: around 65% of students hold full scholarships funded by the state ministry, the Robert Bosch Stiftung and other donors. Sustainability is built into campus life and teaching through partnerships with the city, and the university town of Freiburg offers many community-service projects for the IB's Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) requirement.

UWC RBC does not take Global Selection Programme students, so places are filled only through UWC national committees (and the International Application Pathway). Apply to your national committee for August 2027 entry; the committee assesses financial need after selection.

uwc-mahindra-college.about:
UWC Mahindra College (MUWCI) sits on the hills of rural Maharashtra near Pune, India. Founded in 1997, it has about 238 students aged 16 to 18 who study the two-year IB Diploma Programme on a residential campus.

MUWCI is known for curricular innovation: it pioneered the IB's World Studies Extended Essay and Film Studies, and its signature Experiential Learning Programme and 'MUWCI CORE' are built on four pillars (social and emotional, outdoor and ecological, place-based and contextual, and political). Students help govern campus life, run a Community Fund, stage an annual Theatre Season and work with neighbouring villages through the Akshara Foundation.

For August 2027 entry, apply through your UWC national committee (with need-based scholarships) or, if your family can pay full fees, through the Global Selection Programme, where MUWCI is in the USD 71,000 to 80,000 two-year band, one of the most affordable UWC options.

li-po-chun-uwc-hong-kong.about:
Li Po Chun United World College of Hong Kong (LPCUWC), founded in 1992 as the second UWC in Asia, sits on the green edge of Ma On Shan Country Park, under an hour from central Hong Kong. About 256 students aged 16 to 18 live on campus and take the IB Diploma Programme with average class sizes of 13.

Its Quan Cai ('whole person development') programme hands students responsibility for initiating and running projects and local community service, while Project Week service trips across China and Asia build a deep understanding of the region. The campus combines mountains, trees and beach with easy access to the city.

For August 2027 entry, apply through your UWC national committee (need-based scholarships) or the Global Selection Programme (two-year fee band USD 111,000 to 130,000). LPCUWC also runs UWC short courses.

pearson-college-uwc.about:
Pearson College UWC, founded in 1974 and named after Nobel Peace Prize laureate and former Canadian prime minister Lester B. Pearson, is on the southern tip of Vancouver Island near Victoria, British Columbia, on the traditional territory of the Sc'ianew (Beecher Bay) First Nation. About 200 students aged 16 to 19 from up to 160 countries and every Canadian province live on a forested coastal campus.

Besides the IB Diploma, Pearson offers the Climate Action Leadership Diploma (CALD), an IB Career-related Programme for students who want to specialise in climate leadership. The college is guardian of the Race Rocks Ecological Reserve, so marine science, diving and outdoor learning are part of everyday life.

For August 2027 entry, apply through your UWC national committee (need-based scholarships) or the Global Selection Programme (two-year fee band USD 111,000 to 130,000).

Guardian of the Race Rocks Ecological Reserve: marine science and diving

uwc-changshu-china.about:
UWC Changshu China (UWC CSC), founded in 2015 on the initiative of UWC alumnus Mark Jiapeng Wang, was the first UWC on mainland China. Today it has about 620 students in Grades 10 to 12 (pre-IB and IB Diploma years) in Changshu, Jiangsu province, near Shanghai; most international students join for the two IB Diploma years (Grades 11 and 12).

Every student takes at least one Chinese course (language, literature or culture), so you live in a Mandarin-rich environment. The Zhi Xing ('learning by doing') programme takes students into the wider community, with student leaders running many activities, and environmental work such as recycling, organic farming and wetland protection is part of campus life.

For August 2027 entry, apply through your UWC national committee (need-based scholarships) or the Global Selection Programme (two-year fee band USD 111,000 to 130,000).

uwc-costa-rica.about:
UWC Costa Rica (UWC CR), in Santa Ana near San José, is the only UWC in Latin America and the Caribbean. About 200 students aged 16 to 19 follow a bilingual (English and Spanish) IB Diploma Programme and learn about the region's social, political and cultural history in a country known for peace, democracy, environmental protection and having no army.

Sustainability is the school's guiding framework: it is building a new campus with sustainable construction and nature-reserve restoration. In the Agents of Change Programme, student teams partner with local communities or organisations to design, run and evaluate social-entrepreneurship, activism, technology or science projects, and wellness initiatives support student well-being.

For August 2027 entry, apply through your UWC national committee (need-based scholarships) or the Global Selection Programme (two-year fee band USD 91,000 to 110,000). The school also runs UWC short courses.

uwc-dilijan.about:
UWC Dilijan, opened in 2014 in the forested mountain town of Dilijan, Armenia, is the only UWC in the post-Soviet space. Around 220 students aged about 16 to 19 study the IB Diploma Programme (average class size 14) on a modern campus on the ancient Silk Road, at a crossroads of Europe, the Middle East and Russia.

The school aims to make Dilijan an educational hub for Armenia and the region. Its location and history give students hands-on experience of conflict resolution and peacebuilding, and its 'glocal' approach keeps learning globally relevant but anchored in local reality.

For students from Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Türkiye and the wider region it is the closest UWC. For August 2027 entry, apply through your UWC national committee (need-based scholarships) or the Global Selection Programme (two-year fee band USD 91,000 to 110,000).

uwc-east-africa.about:
UWC East Africa (UWC EA), formerly the International School of Moshi, joined UWC in 2019 as its 18th school. It has two campuses in northern Tanzania: Moshi, with views of Mount Kilimanjaro, and Arusha, overlooking Mount Meru, plus a coastal property in historic Pangani. About 700 students aged 3 to 19 from over 100 nationalities attend; residential students take the IB Diploma Programme on both campuses.

It was Africa's first IB school (1973). The outdoor pursuits programme is built around five streams (Peaks, Plains, Rides, Reefs and Mindfulness), with mountaineering expeditions, off-road adventures, coral-reef restoration and diving.

For August 2027 entry, apply through your UWC national committee (need-based scholarships) or the Global Selection Programme (two-year fee band USD 71,000 to 80,000).

uwc-isak-japan.about:
UWC ISAK Japan, in the mountain resort town of Karuizawa (Nagano), opened in 2014 and became a UWC in 2017. Co-founded by Lin Kobayashi, a Pearson College UWC alumna, it has about 200 students aged 15 to 18 and aims to educate young leaders who become catalysts for positive change.

Its leadership programme combines mindful self-discipline with design innovation and runs through academics, co-curricular life and the dorms. Students start and lead clubs, plan events and help set dorm policies. Japanese language classes and outings (tea ceremony, flower arranging, castles, hot springs, temples) bring Japanese culture into daily life.

IB Diploma students join for the final two years. For August 2027 entry, apply through your UWC national committee (need-based scholarships) or the Global Selection Programme (two-year fee band USD 91,000 to 110,000). ISAK also runs a Summer School for 13 to 14-year-olds.

uwc-mostar.about:
UWC Mostar, founded in 2006, is the only UWC built in a post-conflict country and the first with an explicit aim of helping rebuild a post-conflict society. About 204 students aged 15 to 19 study the IB Diploma in the historic city of Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina, learning to value their differences while promoting equality, tolerance and critical thinking.

Interaction with the local community is the essence of the school: students and staff organise projects and more than 100 events each year that are open to Mostar and the wider community. The school was established by the Foundation Education in Action, which also works on teacher training and education reform in the country.

For August 2027 entry, apply through your UWC national committee (need-based scholarships) or the Global Selection Programme, where UWC Mostar is in the lowest two-year fee band (USD 50,000 to 70,000). It also runs UWC short courses such as Bridging Cultures.

uwc-south-east-asia.about:
UWC South East Asia (UWC SEA) in Singapore is the largest school in the UWC movement, with more than 6,000 students from over 100 countries on two campuses, from kindergarten to Grade 12. It became a full UWC member in 1975 and teaches the IB Diploma in Grades 11 and 12, with residential boarding available from Grade 8.

Students are chosen for deliberate diversity, and the K-12 learning programme links five elements: academics, activities, outdoor education, personal and social education, and service. The Outdoor Education programme includes trips to neighbouring countries across Asia, and Singapore's role as a global hub gives students rich local community links.

UWC SEA does not take Global Selection Programme students. Scholarship places for the two IB years are filled through UWC national committees, so for August 2027 entry contact your national committee (or use the International Application Pathway if you have none and need aid).

uwc-thailand.about:
UWC Thailand (UWCT) sits in the green foothills of Phuket's mountains. It is an IB continuum school from Pre-Kindergarten to Grade 12 with about 540 students; boarding UWC scholars join for the two-year IB Diploma Programme.

Its approach is summed up as 'Good Heart, Balanced Mind, Healthy Body': Social Emotional Learning and mindfulness are built into the curriculum; outdoor education, sport and community engagement develop practical skills; and as a member of the World Academy of Sport it supports elite swimmers and triathletes alongside their studies. Students take part in activities such as coral-reef monitoring.

For August 2027 entry, apply through your UWC national committee (need-based scholarships) or the Global Selection Programme (two-year fee band USD 91,000 to 110,000).

waterford-kamhlaba-uwc.about:
Waterford Kamhlaba UWC of Southern Africa (WK UWCSA) in Mbabane, Eswatini, was founded in 1963 as a direct response to apartheid and was the first multiracial school in Southern Africa. 'Kamhlaba' means 'of the world'. It has about 620 students aged 11 to 20, and UWC scholars join for the two-year IB Diploma Programme.

It is the only UWC on the southern-hemisphere calendar: the school year runs from January to November, so the current selection round is for entry in January 2028. Through community service students work closely with local organisations, including a refugee camp and neighbourhood care points for children.

Apply through your UWC national committee (need-based scholarships) or the Global Selection Programme, where Waterford is in the lowest two-year fee band (USD 50,000 to 70,000).

uwc-global-selection-programme-2027.about:
The UWC Global Selection Programme (GSP) is UWC International's direct-entry route for students who do not need financial aid and want to choose specific UWC schools. It covers 16 of the 18 UWC schools and colleges (all except UWC Robert Bosch College and UWC South East Asia) for the two-year IB Diploma Programme, and the IB Career-related Programme at Pearson College UWC and UWC Maastricht. Studies begin in August 2027 (January 2028 at Waterford Kamhlaba).

The process is fully online and in English: a volunteer selection committee reviews your application, you and your parents may talk with admissions officers from your chosen schools, and shortlisted candidates attend a compulsory online selection day on Zoom with group activities, a project presentation, an interview and a well-being questionnaire. Successful candidates are nominated to one of the schools they listed; the school makes the final offer.

It is the natural route for full fee-paying families in countries without a UWC national committee, including Qatar, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman, as well as anyone who wants to target a particular school. Two-year fees range from USD 50,000 to 70,000 (Adriatic, Mostar, Waterford Kamhlaba) up to USD 155,000 to 165,000 (UWC Atlantic). Applying early matters because places are first-come, first-served.

Fully online selection day in English, no travel needed
Window 3 deadline 5 November 2026; first-come, first-served

You may submit only one UWC application per entry year (GSP or a national committee or the IAP). Applications from Cuba, North Korea, Iran, Sudan, Syria, Russia, Belarus, Crimea and the occupied Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions are listed as "coming soon". Fluent English is not required, but you must manage an English-language online interview.

uwc-international-application-pathway-20.about:
The UWC International Application Pathway (IAP) is UWC International's route for students who expect to need financial support but have no UWC national committee they can apply through, whether because of their nationality or where they live. Successful candidates study the two-year IB Diploma Programme (or the IB Career-related Programme at Pearson College UWC or UWC Maastricht) at one of the UWC schools from August 2027 (January 2028 at Waterford Kamhlaba).

This matters for students in countries without a UWC committee, such as Qatar, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman, as well as residents of other countries who are not covered by any committee. A volunteer selection committee reviews applications, then shortlisted candidates take part in online group and individual activities and interviews in English. Finalists go through a Financial Needs Assessment with their parents' documents, and are nominated to a school based on fit, visa and travel restrictions and the aid available.

Places and funding are limited, so prepare early and submit as soon as the window opens on 23 November 2026.

uwc-short-course-actionxpeace-spain-2026.about:
ActionxPeace (AxP) is a bilingual (English and Spanish) residential short course run by UWC Spain on conflict transformation and peacebuilding. Between 50 and 60 participants aged 15 to 17 from many countries, cultures and backgrounds spend 4 to 8 December 2026 together in Nambroca, near Toledo.

Through interactive workshops, simulations, role-play, games, dialogue sessions and group projects, participants explore identity, empathy, coexistence and how conflicts are interpreted, and practise active listening, non-violent communication, mediation and collaborative problem-solving at personal, community and global level.

It is a short, affordable taste of UWC's mission and a good stepping stone for students thinking of applying to a UWC school.

uwc-short-course-embodying-earth-junior-.about:
Embodying Earth Junior: Learning for a Regenerative Future is a small, closely supervised residential short course for 12 to 14-year-olds at the Núi Tượng Ecological Community in Đồng Nai province, Vietnam, run by UWC Vietnam's short-course team (Education for Good).

Participants spend their days outdoors: forest walks, stories, creative activities, games and quiet reflection help them notice the living world and explore what caring for it means, while shared meals and group living build friendships across backgrounds. By the end they should feel more at home in nature, more confident collaborating and speaking in diverse groups, and equipped with concrete habits for sustainable living.

The course is taught in English and is one of the few UWC programmes open to middle-school students.

uwc-short-course-many-ways-to-be-human-w.about:
Many Ways to be Human is an online UWC short course run by the Svet Peace Project, a nonprofit founded by a UWC Dilijan graduate. Over the winter holidays, an international group of 14 to 19-year-olds meets every other day (26, 28 and 30 December and 1 and 3 January) for 90-minute Socratic seminars on short but deep stories about death, life, beauty and war; past readings include Plato, Russian classics and Nobel laureates from India and Japan.

Students lead the conversation with their own questions; there are no quizzes, research or AI, just one to two hours of reading before each seminar. Each participant designs a 'Svet Project' in their own community (a seminar with friends, an interview, a song, a short film) and receives a personalised certificate and an honest written note on their strengths and areas to grow.

It is an easy, low-cost way to experience UWC-style learning from home during the break.

uwc-short-course-writing-womens-worlds-2.about:
Writing Women’s Worlds is a virtual, cohort-based memoir and creative non-fiction writing programme accredited as a UWC short course and led by writer and theatre practitioner Dr Nandita Dinesh, a UWC Mahindra College alumna who has taught at UWCs in India, Armenia and the USA. The January 2027 cohort runs for twelve weeks, 9 January to 27 March 2027, with workshops on Saturdays 13:00-15:00 US Pacific Time plus one-to-one support.

Participants explore memoir, autobiography and autoethnography, develop their own book project and get advice on publishing pathways. The course is open to all girls and women and is trans-inclusive. Exercises are scaffolded so both first-time and experienced writers benefit.

It suits students who want a serious creative-writing portfolio piece or a published book project, alongside school.

uwc-jordan-selection-2027.about:

Selection is based on merit and potential, not on ability to pay: the committee assesses financial need only after choosing its finalists, and more than 80% of committee-selected students worldwide receive full or partial scholarships covering tuition, boarding, books and IB exams. Students cannot choose their exact school on this route; the committee matches finalists to the places it holds. A JOD 15 fee covers all selection activities.

uwc-yemen-selection-2027.about:
UWC Yemen is the volunteer national committee that represents United World Colleges in Yemen. Each year it selects young people to study the two-year International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme at one of the 18 UWC schools and colleges on four continents, from Armenia and Norway to Hong Kong, Canada and Costa Rica. This round is for entry in August 2027 (Waterford Kamhlaba in Eswatini starts in January 2028).

UWC Yemen's application cycle for 2027 entry opened on 30 August 2026 and closes on 30 November 2026. Documents can be submitted in Arabic or English, and transcripts can be translated without an official sworn translation, which keeps the process accessible.

Selection is based on merit and potential, not on ability to pay: the committee assesses financial need only after choosing its finalists, and more than 80% of committee-selected students worldwide receive full or partial scholarships covering tuition, boarding, books and IB exams. Students cannot choose their exact school on this route; the committee matches finalists to the places it holds.
highlights: Deadline 30 November 2026
Need-based scholarships: more than 80% of committee-selected students get aid
Places at UWC schools on four continents, IB Diploma from August 2027
uwc-yemen-selection-2027.eligibility: Yemeni students in the last years of secondary school who meet UWC Yemen's eligibility criteria (see ye.uwc.org); documents may be in Arabic or English. Only one UWC application per entry year is allowed (national committee, Global Selection Programme or International Application Pathway).
how_to_apply: Check the eligibility criteria and UWC Yemen selection process on ye.uwc.org.
Download and complete the Application Form linked on ye.uwc.org/how-to-apply.
Prepare transcripts and documents in Arabic or English (simple, non-sworn translation is accepted).
Submit the complete application by 30 November 2026.
Shortlisted applicants take part in the selection stages; finalists complete a financial assessment and are nominated to a UWC school.
uwc-yemen-selection-2027.costs: Applying is free unless stated otherwise. Scholarships are need-based and set after a financial assessment; they range from partial to full (tuition, room, board, books, IB exams) and sometimes all-inclusive (travel and pocket money).

flex-global-2027-28.about:
FLEX Global is a highly competitive, merit-based exchange funded by the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs and implemented by American Councils for International Education with AFS, Amideast and iEARN. It builds on more than 30 years of the Future Leaders Exchange (FLEX) and almost 25 years of the Kennedy-Lugar Youth Exchange and Study (YES) programme, which have now been merged into one global programme. Finalists spend the 2027-28 academic year in the United States: they live with a screened volunteer host family, attend a U.S. high school, do community activities and take part in 'American Excellence' enrichment on business, technology, entrepreneurship, government and U.S. history.

Eligible citizens (2027-28): Argentina, Armenia, Bahrain, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil, Egypt, Georgia, Greece, India, Indonesia, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Kosovo, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Mongolia, Montenegro, Morocco, North Macedonia, Pakistan, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Tajikistan, Thailand, Tunisia, Türkiye, Turkmenistan, Ukraine and Uzbekistan. Qatar, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Oman are not on the list; Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Hungary and Slovakia are not recruiting this cycle.

Selection runs in rounds: English testing, proctored essays, interviews with FLEX staff and a full application; final selection is made in the U.S., with English only one factor among several. Finalists pass a medical check, learn their status in spring 2027, attend a pre-departure orientation in June or July and fly to the U.S. in August 2027. Georgia, Armenia, Kazakhstan, Ukraine and other first-wave countries closed in October 2026; Balkan, Greek, Jordanian, Moroccan, Bahraini, Brazilian and Tunisian applicants can still apply in November 2026.

cbyx-high-school-2027-28.about:
The Congress-Bundestag Youth Exchange (CBYX) is jointly funded by the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs and the German Bundestag. For more than 40 years it has sent over 30,000 young people between the two countries. In 2027-28, 210 American high school students will live with German host families, attend a local German high school and learn German through daily life.

Scholars also visit the Bundestag, meet officials, join intercultural seminars and travel within Germany. No previous German is needed. The programme is run in each U.S. state by AFS-USA, CIEE or YFU-USA, and alumni join the State Department exchange-alumni network and the CBYX Alumni Association.

The extended application deadline is 3 November 2026 (11:59 pm Pacific); selection runs from January to April and results are announced between March and May 2027.
highlights: 210 fully funded scholarships for a year in Germany
Bundestag visit and intercultural seminars
No prior German required; extended deadline 3 November 2026
cbyx-high-school-2027-28.eligibility: U.S. citizens aged 15 to 18.5 on 1 August 2027 (born 1 February 2009 to 1 August 2012); current high school students with a GPA of 2.5 or higher; interested in learning German and representing the U.S. Designed for students who have not lived abroad for six months or longer in the last five years.
how_to_apply: Go to usagermanyscholarship.org and select your state to see your implementing organisation.
Complete the online application before 11:59 pm Pacific on 3 November 2026.
Take part in the selection process (January-April 2027), including interviews.
Selection announcements come between March and May 2027; pre-departure orientation follows.
cbyx-high-school-2027-28.costs: Scholarship covers international travel, host family placement, school enrolment, orientation and seminars, health insurance and programme activities, funded by the U.S. and German governments.

cbyx-young-professionals-2027-28.about:
The Congress-Bundestag Youth Exchange for Young Professionals, run by Cultural Vistas for 40 years, offers 65 Americans (and 65 Germans in the other direction) a year of study, work and cultural immersion. It has three phases: eight weeks of intensive German at language schools across Germany (August-September); a semester of classes in your career field at a university, technical or professional school (October-January); and a three-to-five-month internship in a German-speaking workplace (February-June).

It especially welcomes applicants from business, engineering, technical, vocational and agricultural fields, though all fields with relevant experience are considered. No prior German is required. Participants live with hosts, in apartments or in dorms.

Applications for the next programme year must be submitted by 1 November.
highlights: Study semester plus paid-or-unpaid internship in Germany
Two months of intensive German included
Funded flights, tuition, housing (pre-internship) and stipend
cbyx-young-professionals-2027-28.eligibility: U.S. citizens aged 18.5 to 24 on 1 August of the programme start year; high school graduates with a diploma; clear career goals and relevant work or internship experience; strong interest in Germany and world affairs. Prior German is not required. State Department employment and prior-exchange rules apply.
how_to_apply: Request an application on the Cultural Vistas CBYX page; the team verifies eligibility and sends a link.
Upload your resume, transcript and other documents and complete the online form.
Submit everything by 1 November 2026.
Shortlisted candidates are interviewed; finalists are placed in Germany for the following programme year.
cbyx-young-professionals-2027-28.costs: Covered: round-trip airfare from Washington, DC, two months of language school, one semester of tuition, housing before the internship, a monthly living stipend, programme travel in Germany and German health insurance. Funding during the internship depends on the internship salary; Cultural Vistas recommends having about USD 5,000 for other costs.

intercultura-afs-italy-2027-28.about:
Intercultura is Italy's leading non-profit for international school exchanges and the Italian member of the AFS network, with more than 70 years of experience. Italian secondary school students can spend a year, semester or shorter period abroad in 2027-28, living with a volunteer host family and attending a local school, with volunteers supporting them before, during and after the experience.

About two out of three participants leave with a scholarship. Intercultura's own scholarships cover from 25% to 100% of the participation fee, and hundreds more are funded by companies, foundations, banks and the INPS ITACA programme for children of public employees.

Registration for 2027/2028 programmes closes on 10 November 2026, followed by selection with volunteers in local centres.
highlights: Two in three participants receive a scholarship
Scholarships from 25% to 100% of the fee
Part of the worldwide AFS network
intercultura-afs-italy-2027-28.eligibility: Secondary school students resident in Italy within the age and school-year ranges set in Intercultura's 2027/2028 call; some scholarships are tied to region, school or parents' employer (e.g., INPS ITACA).
how_to_apply: Read the 2027/2028 brochure and programme list on intercultura.it.
Register online for school programmes abroad before 10 November 2026.
Apply for Intercultura, partner or INPS scholarships as part of registration.
Take part in the selection with local volunteers.
intercultura-afs-italy-2027-28.costs: Participation fee varies by destination and length; Intercultura scholarships cover 25-100% of it, and partner scholarships add further support.

afs-turkiye-school-programs-2027-28.about:
The Türk Kültür Vakfı (Turkish Culture Foundation) is AFS's partner in Türkiye. Through AFS School Programmes, students spend time in another country living with carefully chosen volunteer families and attending a local high school, joining daily life like a member of the community.

For 2027-28 there are year-long programmes and short school programmes in three windows: a three-month programme (September to December 2027), the autumn 2027 term and the spring 2028 term. Services include orientation camps before departure, during the stay and on return, 24/7 support, school placement and visa assistance, and access to the AFS alumni network. AFS Türkiye also runs AFS Global You Adventurer, an online exchange for 14 to 17-year-olds.

Applications for the first interview period close at 23:59 on 12 November 2026; a second interview period follows.
highlights: Year, term and 3-month school programmes worldwide
Orientation camps and 24/7 AFS support
First deadline 12 November 2026
afs-turkiye-school-programs-2027-28.eligibility: Citizens of Türkiye or holders of a long-term residence permit issued by Türkiye, enrolled in a Ministry of National Education secondary school, within the age range in the 2027-2028 application guide.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027-2028 application guide on turkkulturvakfi.org.tr.
Fill in the AFS Programmes 2027-2028 application form and pay the application fee.
Submit by 12 November 2026, 23:59, to join the first interview period (a later deadline applies to the second).
Attend the interviews and selection activities; selected students attend orientation before departure.
afs-turkiye-school-programs-2027-28.costs: Programme fees are listed in the FAQ on the AFS Türkiye page and vary by country and length. Included services include school placement, host family, orientations, support and visa assistance; pocket money and personal expenses are extra.
